newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude prices rise, but market sleepy.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude prices rise, but market sleepy.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes rose Monday with benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI), as regional spot trade failed to get started after last week's jump in discounts, traders said.
The sharp increase in the discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) had players sidestepping the market Monday as they reconsidered the appropriate price for the next deal.
Exxon sold a 400,000 barrel cargo of ANS crude Friday at $1.32 off WTI Friday.
The discount for ANS stands 0.27 cents a barrel lower than the previous deal done April 4.
Outright prices at $18.48/18.68 a barrel Monday, five cents higher than Friday.
Heavy imports of South American crude for May have undercut the price of competing ANS, now offered at $0.95 cents a barrel, buyers claimed.
Texaco is expecting another load of Colombian South Blend, an ANS substitute, to be delivered to its Washington state refinery, May 20, traders said.
ARCO on Monday looked to buy Wilmington (THUMS) crude oil for May, after traders said the company's production fell short of supply obligations.
Line 63 and California heavy crude markets remained well- supplied, with no deals reported early.
